picks.showTitle: Tehillim for the Soul with Dr. Miriam Menaker
picks.title: Rosh Hashanah: The Birth of a New You with Dr. Miriam Menaker

picks.reason: Explores Rosh Hashanah as a time for personal renewal and partnership with God.

picks.showTitle: Tehillim for the Soul with Dr. Miriam Menaker
picks.title: When I Am Not There Anymore: The Spiritual Secret of Rosh Hashanah with Dr. Miriam Menaker
picks.summary: "When I reach the moment that I am not there anymore."A pianist was once asked how he knows he has truly succeeded in a performance. His answer: it is when the instrument becomes the musician — when there is no separation between the player and the music. He is one with it.That single idea captures the entire spiritual journey of Rosh Hashanah.In this deeply moving episode, we explore one of the most profound teachings in Jewish mysticism: why the shofar falls silent when Rosh Hashanah meets Shabbat. picks.reason: Explores Jewish mystical teachings on the spiritual silence of the shofar on Rosh Hashanah.

picks.showTitle: Entering Rosh Hashanah with Rav Shlomo Katz
picks.title: The Rosh Hashanah Secret Hidden in the Shofar's Narrow End
picks.summary: We spend so much of our lives trying.We work on our marriages. We work on our children. We work on our parnasah, our Torah, ourselves. picks.reason: Jewish teaching on effort, success, and humility during Rosh Hashanah season.

picks.title: Taller On The Inside - Rabbi Deborah Silver
picks.summary: The High Holyday liturgy is full of images of emptiness and abasement, as if to tell us, “You got nothing.”  How does this week’s parashah, always read just before the High Holydays, put itself into conversation with Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur?
picks.reason: Connects the weekly Torah portion to themes of emptiness and humility before the High Holidays.

picks.showTitle: The Daily Derech from Exploring Judaism
picks.title: The Present Moment | September 7th, 2026
picks.summary: See today's text here!In this episode of The Daily Derech, Rabbi Marcus Rubenstein explores the Rosh Hashanah Torah readings, Hilchot Shofar, and a teaching from Menorat HaMaor about repentance and returning to God.The Parashah section examines Hagar and Ishmael being sent into the wilderness and saved after God hears the boy’s cry. Through Rashi’s interpretation, Rabbi Rubenstein emphasizes that Ishmael was judged according to who he was in that moment, highlighting the importance of sincere repentance and our present actions.The Rambam section explains the Torah obligation to hear the shofar
picks.reason: Discusses repentance and divine judgment through Rashi's interpretation of Torah readings for Rosh Hashanah.

picks.summary: These classes teach the day’s section of the weekly Torah portion. The lesson is taught using the original Hebrew text with the indispensable commentary of Rashi—both translated and elucidated so that anyone can follow along.

picks.title: Rambam: Ishut, Chapter 16
picks.summary: Rabbi Gordon studies one chapter a day from Maimonides’ classic legal work of Mishneh Torah. The original Hebrew text is read and then translated and clearly explained in English.
picks.reason: Clear study of Rambam's Mishneh Torah on Jewish law and ethics in marriage.

picks.title: Chullin 129 - September 6, 24 Elul
picks.summary: A braita rules that if one cuts an olive-bulk of flesh from a limb attached to a living animal, designating it for food only after cutting renders it pure, whereas designating it prior to cutting renders it susceptible to food impurity, as it touches the limb (which has high level impurity) as it is being cut. The Gemara presents Rav Asi's challenge to Rabbi Zeira as to why prior designation causes impurity, given that the cut site is a concealed place
picks.reason: Talmudic analysis of ritual purity laws related to living animals.

picks.title: Hullin 133: Abaye's Priestly Gifts
picks.summary: Rav Yosef tested Rava and Abaye, regarding the gifts that are supposed to go to the kohen - when the kohen grabs the goods, he presents himself with the defense of obtaining the materials. Abaye explains how he used to reach of the gifts, but was schooled by others to simply wait. Plus, did Abaye teach Torah when he should have been functioning as a kohen? Also, partnered ownership of animals with an idolator -- how far can that be taken?
picks.reason: Talmudic discussion on priestly gifts and Abaye's conduct as a kohen.

picks.title: This Is Your Life - Rabbi Hannah Jensen | Erev Rosh Hashanah Sermon
picks.summary: Don't let your life pass you by. It may be that your life is not what you imagined. Grieve what you need to grieve about where you are. And then invest in the life you have and find the beauty in it.
picks.reason: Rosh Hashanah sermon on grief, life meaning, and embracing present reality.
